chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Jamming with Ellington men and Fats Waller at the hotel
summary: He recalls Lawrence Brown, Cootie Williams, Johnny Hodges, Arthur Whetsel and Harry Carney, and Fats Waller with a rented organ.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Who did you jam with in Duke's band?
Oh, Lawrence and I used to get together, and Cootie, Cootie was younger then. He liked to play a lot, you know, and he'd play a lot. And, of course, Johnny didn't,

he didn't do too much jamming around. And Johnny was always kind of quiet back there in those times to me. But Duke had a trumpet player -- Whetsel, Arthur Whetsel. Chief we called him. He used to love to play. He played soft, mute and pretty things, you know. Harry Carney -- always had a lot of fun with Carney back in those times.

He didn't jam much but he'd come around. No, he didn't do much jamming. Johnny didn't either. Johnny didn't as a rule. He -- Johnny could play with anything, but he didn't care for it as a rule. He's very quiet, you know, off by himself. And Lawrence didn't as a rule jam, but we would just get together and exchange ideas, you know, a few things.

Duke's band worked so hard I guess they didn't care about doing a lot of playing. But a lot of groups used to come in there, they'd always play. Fats Waller used to -- when he'd come in that hotel, he used to get a little organ -- have them bring up a little organ up there. And he'd play it and nobody didn't do a lot of jamming with him. They'd just listen to him play and sing. You know, he's a lot of fun. And he was always writing, so he kept a piano or a little organ around him all the time.
He'd rent, you know, yeah. Bring it up

to his room. Yeah, this -- this -- I forgot the name. Isn't that strange -- of that little hotel. But anybody would know it. It was right -- it was the only place you could stay almost around in there. A lot of those bands would come and play the Regal Theater, and the Regal Theater had good shows in there all the time.
